title: Phelipeaux d'Herbault (Paris) to Philippe de Béthune (Rome), 13 February 1626, BnF fr. 3669 no. 25 (read from its twin no. 26)

documents.shelfmark: BnF Français 3669 no. 25, ff. 69-71 (Gallica btv1b9060205q, canvases 74-76); twin copy no. 26, ff. 72-74 (canvases 77-79)

plaintext.source: No. 26 (ff. 72-74) is the same letter with the same cipher runs at the same points, deciphered between the lines by a contemporary hand.

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF images (black-and-white microfilm openings); the reading transcribes the clear text and the interlinear decipherment of no. 26
transcription.notes: The ciphertext was not transcribed group by group; only the opening of run 1 (to 92 g 17 ᴢ 43 x cu 4 7 ᴢ ᵈ p x ᴣ ᴣ 6 ᵷ x) and the end of run 3 (… 68 93 …) are given, so no token count. NOTES: the two clerks' figures 'are read differently at this resolution'.

system.summary: Nomenclator of one- to three-character groups mixing Arabic figures and letter-forms, about 18 groups for 48 plaintext letters in the first run, so most groups stand for syllables or words.
system.sibling_key: The volume holds about thirty further letters of 1625-26 in the same cipher, nearly all glossed; not used to tabulate a key.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary interlinear decipherment on the twin copy, BnF fr. 3669 no. 26 (ff. 72-74)

tools: fetch.sh, region.sh, zoom.sh (Gallica IIIF openings and zoomed regions)

solution.what: Fetched the Gallica IIIF manifest of fr. 3669 and the openings for pieces 24-27; fixed canvas = folio + 5 on ff. 70 and 73.
Catalogue task: check whether no. 26 is the decipherment of no. 25.

Clear text of nos. 25 and 26 compared: identical word for word; cipher runs fall after the same clear words; groups match at the two points checked (run 1 opening, run 3 ending). No group-for-group identity claimed.
Transcribed the letter with the interlinear decipherment of no. 26 for each cipher run (ct/letter_13feb1626.md); two proper names and 'Soubise' uncertain, a few glossed stretches left as '…'.

outcome.notes: Read at the time: the reading is the contemporary decipherment on the twin copy, not an independent decryption. Unread in ct/letter_13feb1626.md: one whole run after 'les Anglois et les autres' ([chiffre: …]), ellipses inside the first and last passages; uncertain: Santriny, Montembelans, Soubise. Whether the letter or the series is in print was not checked.
